summary: Walker (benten-core subgraph_spec) is sound: BFS-canonical-path enumeration is deterministic + byte-lex tie-broken via BTreeMap edge iteration, fail-closed on unresolvable roots + self-referential specs, walker_as_subgraph preserves CLAUDE.md #1 12-primitive irreducibility (READ/TRANSFORM/BRANCH/ITERATE only, ≥4 OperationNodes, byte-stable canonical-bytes, handler_id pinned). RestrictedScope 6-dim containment is decidable (no fixpoint) + composable (&&-composed per-dim; inverse-direction on label_denylist correctly modeled). Chain validator non-widening fires for both Hashes (Vec subset) + RestrictedSelector arms; cross-arm transitions explicit-reject as non-comparable. No `OpaqueSelector` arm; structural backstop via tf3b_no_opaque_selector_arm_structural; Scope is deliberately NOT `#[non_exhaustive]` so a third-arm proposal compile-breaks at every consumer site (the freeze contract). However, FIVE substantive R6 findings: (1) MAJOR — `scope` field on AuthorizationGrant is NOT covered by `binding_message`; an attacker who obtains a grant can replace `scope` with a wider RestrictedScope and the binding-sig still verifies — the wave-3e ALPN handler ARM 6 reads the (now-attacker-supplied) `scope`, admitting requests outside the issuer-intended allowlist. (2) MAJOR — `issuer_verifying_key` is also NOT in `binding_message`; a self-attesting grant can be re-signed end-to-end by an attacker who substitutes their own pubkey, bypassing the issuer-identity defense entirely (the wave-3e handler trusts the grant's self-carried vk; no out-of-band RotationLog cross-check at v1-beta). (3) MINOR — ARM-1 `unresolved_peer` short-circuit reads UCAN field BEFORE ARM-5 binding-sig validation, a literal contravention of RATIFIED-S&C §R3 'check binding_sig BEFORE consulting the UCAN scope or key material — the binding is the foundation'; runtime is operationally reasonable (must resolve who's asking first) but the §R3 deviation is not documented in V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE.md 15.d or SECURITY-POSTURE.md. (4) MINOR — `UcanEnvelope.unresolved_peer` sentinel field is being frozen as part of the v1-beta wire format despite phase-4-backlog.md:175 naming a P-III decision-point at G-CORE-9 freeze time; that decision was NOT taken at G-CORE-9 (no row in V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE-DEFERRED.md, no ratification in V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE.md 15.d). The field is being silently frozen as-is; either ratify the keep decision in 15.d or add a V1-FROZEN-DEFERRED row. (5) OBS — `Spec` derives `Deserialize` but has no `from_canonical_bytes` constructor + no post-deserialize re-sort of `roots`; a CBOR-deserialized Spec from unsorted roots will produce a non-canonical CID. No live attack surface (Spec not embedded in wire formats at v1-beta) but the API design has the hazard. Plus 3 OBS doc-coupling items.

findings.title: AuthorizationGrant.scope is post-sign-mutable — binding_message does NOT cover scope, allowing scope-widening attack on v1-beta
evidence: crates/benten-caps/src/authorization_grant.rs:359-375 `binding_message` includes ONLY (BINDING_SIG_DOMAIN || ucan_cbor || km_cbor || audience.as_bytes()) — scope is NOT in the message

crates/benten-caps/src/authorization_grant.rs:477-486 `issue_for_test` constructs the grant with `scope: Some(scope)` set OUTSIDE the binding_sig computation (binding_message is called at line 472 with only ucan/km/audience_cid; scope is attached at line 484 post-sign)
crates/benten-caps/src/authorization_grant.rs:591-625 `verify_binding` re-checks ONLY the 3 signed components; scope is never validated by the cryptographic binding

crates/benten-sync/src/ucan_blobs_protocol.rs:499-519 ARM 6 reads `request.grant.scope` (the post-sign-mutable field) to authorize the ciphertext_hash request — attacker who obtains any grant can present it with a fresh wider `scope: with_hashes([X, attacker_targeted_hashes...])` and ARM 6 admits

Attack: Alice issues grant G to Bob for hash X with scope=Some(with_hashes([X])); Bob's grant body is observed by attacker A in transit (or A is Bob); A presents G to provider P with scope swapped to with_hashes([X, Y]); P's handler runs ARM 5 verify_binding (PASSES — scope not in binding_message), then ARM 6 admits the request for Y; A has exfiltrated bytes for Y the issuer never authorized.

RATIFIED-S&C §R3 explicit: 'binding_sig is the issuer's signature over the CBOR-encoded `(ucan, key_material)` tuple bound to the same audience' — at the time §R3 was written, `scope` lived inside the UCAN envelope (per the wave-3b shape); the wave-3e refactor split `scope: Option<RestrictedScope>` to AuthorizationGrant top-level WITHOUT carrying it into the binding-sig coverage. This is a §R3 conformance regression introduced by the 3b → 3e split.
findings.disposition: FIX-NOW (HARD RULE 12 — substantive security regression introduced by 3b→3e split; closes a wide-scope-substitution attack class)
findings.remediation: Extend `binding_message` to include the scope: `binding_message(ucan, key_material, audience, scope: Option<&RestrictedScope>) -> Vec<u8>` (4-component CBOR concatenation). Update all `issue_*_for_test` constructors + production `issue_for_test` to thread scope into the signed payload. Update `verify_binding` to re-construct the message with `self.scope.as_ref()`. Mint a tf3b_scope_substitution_post_sign_rejected pin: issue grant G with scope_A; clone G + swap scope to scope_B (wider); verify_binding returns BindingMismatch. Per pim-2 §3.6b sub-rule-4 substantive-arm coverage. CATALOG impact: NONE (BindingMismatch arm already covers; no new ErrorCode needed). If implementation prefers to leave scope out of binding-sig for backward compatibility, then explicit MAJOR-equivalent V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE 15.d ratification record + SECURITY-POSTURE.md Compromise registry entry stating 'scope is post-sign-mutable; the provider's ARM 6 trust boundary IS the entire scope-narrowing defense; abuse requires both grant-theft AND provider-cooperation' — but this is the WEAK option and undermines the wave-3e R3 'binding is the foundation' contract.

findings.title: AuthorizationGrant.issuer_verifying_key is self-attesting + not in binding_message + no out-of-band cross-check at v1-beta — key-substitution attack bypasses the binding-sig defense entirely
evidence: crates/benten-caps/src/authorization_grant.rs:246-252 `issuer_verifying_key: Vec<u8>` carries the verifying key the validator uses for binding-sig verification
crates/benten-caps/src/authorization_grant.rs:359-375 `binding_message` does NOT include `issuer_verifying_key` — it's outside the signed payload

crates/benten-caps/src/authorization_grant.rs:600-625 `verify_binding` uses `self.issuer_verifying_key` to construct the VerifyingKey and verify the sig — the grant attests to its own issuer-pubkey with no cross-check

crates/benten-sync/src/ucan_blobs_protocol.rs:288-291 explicit docstring: 'The handler validates grants signed by OTHER issuers via the embedded `issuer_verifying_key` on the grant' — confirms v1-beta has NO out-of-band issuer-vk lookup; the only DID-based identity resolution is the ARM 1 `unresolved_peer` SENTINEL flag, not a real RotationLog query

Attack: attacker A obtains plaintext grant bytes for hash X; A generates a fresh Ed25519 keypair (vk_A, sk_A); A constructs a new grant with same (ucan, key_material, audience_cid) — re-signs binding_message with sk_A — sets issuer_verifying_key = vk_A.to_bytes(); A presents to provider P. P's verify_binding PASSES (the binding-sig is mathematically valid against vk_A; the message bytes match); ARM 1-6 all pass with no issuer-identity check. The result: P treats this as a valid grant attributed to vk_A even though the LEGITIMATE issuer (vk_alice) never authorized this grant — defeating the binding-sig defense's entire purpose.

Mitigating context: the cipher key_material.bytes IS the real protection — A cannot decrypt the served ciphertext without the actual key material. So the attack does NOT directly compromise confidentiality. BUT: (a) it lets A enumerate which ciphertexts a provider holds (existence-oracle), (b) it lets A consume provider bandwidth + may trigger rate-limit DoS, (c) it falsely attributes the request to vk_A in any provider audit log — provenance corruption, (d) if any future operation depends on issuer-identity-as-authority (manifest envelopes, plugin caps), the substitution propagates

RATIFIED-S&C §R3 says the binding is the foundation — but the foundation rests on trusting `issuer_verifying_key`, which is self-attesting. The ratification implicitly assumed out-of-band issuer-vk verification; the wave-3e implementation deferred it without naming the gap. SECURITY-POSTURE.md:2552-2555 only names the unresolved_peer sentinel replacement, not the full issuer-vk cross-check
findings.disposition: FIX-NOW (HARD RULE 12 — name the gap explicitly + decide remediation at this R6) OR BELONGS-NAMED-NOW (V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE-DEFERRED.md row + SECURITY-POSTURE.md Compromise entry; G-COMP-1 destination for the RotationLog wire-up)
findings.remediation: Two-part: (1) name the v1-beta security limit explicitly: add V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE-DEFERRED.md row 'AuthorizationGrant.issuer_verifying_key out-of-band RotationLog cross-check' with G-COMP-1 destination ARM 1 swap (the sentinel → RotationLog::resolve substitution per docs/SECURITY-POSTURE.md:2552-2555 — but EXPANDED to include `assert!(resolved_issuer_vk == grant.issuer_verifying_key)` cross-check); (2) add SECURITY-POSTURE.md Compromise registry entry naming the attack class + the provenance/existence-oracle/DoS impact + the v1-beta mitigation (ARM 1 sentinel + audience-binding via ARM 2 narrows the attack-class to provider-cooperative scenarios) + the production fix wire-up. Without (1)+(2), the v1-beta wire-format freeze locks the self-attestation pattern without ratifying its security posture — a freeze without an accompanying threat-model record. The proper structural fix (signed-issuer-vk OR mandatory RotationLog cross-check at handler ARM 1) is too large for R6 fix-pass; explicit naming + Compromise registry is the right cut.

findings.title: Handler ARM 1 (unresolved_peer) fires BEFORE ARM 5 (binding-sig) — literal contravention of RATIFIED-S&C §R3 'check binding_sig BEFORE consulting the UCAN scope or key material'
evidence: crates/benten-sync/src/ucan_blobs_protocol.rs:423-433 ARM 1: `if request.grant.ucan.unresolved_peer { return Err(UcanBlobsHandlerError::UnresolvedDeny { ... }); }` — reads a UCAN envelope field
crates/benten-sync/src/ucan_blobs_protocol.rs:487-497 ARM 5: `request.grant.verify_binding(...)` — the binding-sig check

RATIFIED-sharing-and-confidentiality-2026-05-21.md §R3 explicit: 'Validators check binding_sig BEFORE consulting the UCAN scope or the key material — the binding is the foundation.' ARM 1 reads `request.grant.ucan.unresolved_peer` — that IS consulting the UCAN (the field lives on UcanEnvelope). The wording 'BEFORE consulting the UCAN' is being literally violated.

Operational rationale (per the codified mr2 disposition in r5-g-core-3e-mini-review.json): 'cannot-validate-binding-if-cannot-resolve-peer' — if the peer-DID is unresolvable the validator has no basis to trust the issuer-vk regardless of binding-sig validity. This is REASONABLE — but the §R3 ordering is still being violated literally + the deviation rationale is not documented in V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE.md 15.d or SECURITY-POSTURE.md

Confirmed: docstring at authorization_grant.rs:96-122 was already retensed (per mr2) to acknowledge ARM-1-before-ARM-5 ordering, but the ratification record at V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE.md 15.d still cites '§R3 binding is the foundation' without naming the ARM-1 short-circuit exception

Coupled fixture issue (mr7): issue_with_unresolved_peer_for_test at authorization_grant.rs:496-519 mutates ucan.unresolved_peer post-sign, producing a binding-sig-INVALID grant that passes ARM 1 (UnresolvedDeny) before reaching ARM 5; test discriminator-asserts `matches!(result, UnresolvedDeny)` (safety net) — but the fixture is brittle to future ARM-reorder. mr7 carry filed at phase-4-backlog.md:176
findings.disposition: FIX-NOW (HARD RULE 12 — V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE 15.d ratification record needs the ARM-1 exception named; pure documentation/ratification fix, no code change)
findings.remediation: Amend V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE.md 15.d 'Frozen semantics' bullet 'Validators check `binding_sig` BEFORE consulting the UCAN scope or the key material' to add: 'EXCEPTION: an unresolvable-peer-DID short-circuit (ARM 1 in the wave-3e handler at ucan_blobs_protocol.rs:423-433) MAY fire before binding-sig verification when the issuer-DID cannot be resolved (because no binding-sig check could be meaningful without a way to trust the issuer-vk regardless). This is the operational pre-condition to §R3, not a violation. The unresolvable-peer flag is itself bound by binding_sig (it lives in UcanEnvelope CBOR shape; tampering invalidates binding_sig), so an attacker cannot SET the flag without invalidating; the short-circuit only fires for grants legitimately marked unresolved-peer by the issuer.' Cross-link to SECURITY-POSTURE.md per the ratification-against-drift §3.6h discipline.

findings.title: UcanEnvelope.unresolved_peer P-III decision was NAMED for G-CORE-9 freeze time but NOT TAKEN at G-CORE-9 — field is silently frozen as-is without ratification record or deferred-row

findings.title: Spec derives Deserialize without from_canonical_bytes API + no post-deserialize re-sort of roots — CBOR-deserialized Spec with unsorted roots produces non-canonical CID
evidence: crates/benten-core/src/subgraph_spec/spec.rs:189 `#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)] pub struct Spec { roots: Vec<Cid>, edges: BTreeMap<Cid, BTreeMap<String, Cid>>, inclusion: SubgraphSpecRestriction, max_depth: u32 }`

crates/benten-core/src/subgraph_spec/spec.rs:403-432 SpecBuilder::build is the ONLY constructor path that sorts roots (line 412-415: `let mut roots: Vec<Cid> = self.roots.into_iter().collect(); roots.sort_by_key(|c| *c.as_bytes());`)
No from_canonical_bytes constructor exists on Spec (only to_canonical_bytes at lines 251-253); serde Deserialize bypasses build()

Hazard: code that calls `serde_ipld_dagcbor::from_slice::<Spec>(bytes)` with unsorted roots gets a Spec whose internal roots Vec is in the deserialized order. spec.cid() at lines 260-264 calls to_canonical_bytes which encodes the Vec in declared order — producing a DIFFERENT CID than the producer's canonical form. AuthorizationGrant.audience_binding-style invariants that depend on Spec.cid() stability would silently break.

Mitigating context: at HEAD, Spec is not embedded in any wire format (verified: no `serde_*::from_*::<Spec>` call sites in production source; only test code constructs via builder); the engine wrapper at engine_share_scope.rs:59 takes `&Spec` by reference. So the hazard is not live at v1-beta. But the API design has the hazard — any future wave that embeds Spec in CBOR (e.g. AuthorizationGrant.spec_selector future field, or Drop bundle subgraph_spec carry) introduces a CID-instability bug class

Comparison: AuthorizationGrant.from_canonical_bytes at authorization_grant.rs:646-649 IS provided + delegates to serde without re-sort, but the AuthorizationGrant struct uses primitive fields without sortable invariants. Spec is qualitatively different (its CID is content-derived + load-bearing)
findings.disposition: BELONGS-NAMED-NOW (V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE-DEFERRED.md row — name the post-deserialize-canonicalization hardening; G-COMP-1 destination since no live attack at v1-beta) OR FIX-NOW (add a `from_canonical_bytes_validating` constructor that re-runs SpecBuilder.sort + cid-stability check — ~15 LOC)
findings.remediation: Option 1 (NAME-NOW, recommended): add V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE-DEFERRED.md row 'Spec post-deserialize canonicalization' under G-COMP-1 with shape: ship a `Spec::from_canonical_bytes(bytes) -> Result<Spec, SubgraphSpecError>` that decodes via serde + reconstructs via SpecBuilder (forcing re-sort) + asserts `cid_post_reconstruction == cid_pre_reconstruction`. ~30 LOC + golden test. Anchor: this finding. Option 2 (FIX-NOW): same constructor in benten-core::subgraph_spec; covers the hazard before any wave embeds Spec in CBOR. Recommend Option 1 since no consumer exists; Option 2 is justified if any near-term G-COMP work touches Spec serialization.

findings.title: Walker INTENTIONALLY skips SubgraphSpecRestriction::ByLabel filtering — every BFS-reached CID emitted regardless of Inclusion predicate; doc names the downstream filter site but no consumer at HEAD actually applies the filter
evidence: crates/benten-core/src/subgraph_spec/walker.rs:134-142 explicit comment: 'For v1: SubgraphSpecRestriction::Unrestricted always passes; SubgraphSpecRestriction::ByLabel narrows but is evaluated against labels carried by the Spec's structural definition — at the walker substrate level we emit every BFS-reached CID and leave label-based filtering to downstream resolvers that have access to the actual Node bodies.'
Verified: no downstream consumer of WalkResult applies a ByLabel filter at HEAD (greppable: walk_share_scope at engine_share_scope.rs:59-62 returns WalkResult unchanged; no resolver consumes it yet)

Consequence: a Spec built with `with_label_allowlist(['Recipe'])` produces a walk that includes Nodes of ALL labels, not just 'Recipe'. The Inclusion-dim narrowing is structurally PRESENT (Spec.contains_spec uses it correctly for combinator semantics) but functionally INERT at the walker boundary

Per RATIFIED-S&C §R4 BFS-order canonical-path contract: paths are a wire-format invariant — emitting wider-than-intended Nodes doesn't break path canonicalization, but it does break recipient-side expectations if the recipient reasons 'I got Node X in WalkResult therefore Spec admitted X by inclusion predicate' (they should not reason that at v1-beta but the API shape invites the misreading)

Not a security bug — but a clarity gap: the walker IS the BFS substrate; resolvers above it apply Inclusion. At v1-beta there ARE no resolvers above it. The freeze locks the substrate-emits-everything contract
findings.disposition: BELONGS-NAMED-NOW (V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE.md 15.h or 15.a clarification + V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE-DEFERRED.md downstream-Inclusion-filter row for G-COMP-1)
findings.remediation: Two doc edits: (a) V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE.md 15.h 'Frozen surfaces' bullet add: '`walker::walk` is the BFS-enumeration substrate ONLY — it does NOT apply Spec.inclusion (SubgraphSpecRestriction::ByLabel) filtering. The walker emits every BFS-reachable (Cid, StructuralPath); downstream resolvers (G-COMP-1: subgraph-shape-evaluator) apply the Inclusion predicate against actual Node bodies. findings.title: chain_validator cross-arm transition (Hashes ↔ RestrictedSelector) returns false (typed ChainNotNarrowing) but rationale isn't surfaced at the public API — consumers can't distinguish 'cross-arm not yet supported' from 'genuinely widening'
evidence: crates/benten-caps/src/chain_validator.rs:100-105 `(Scope::Hashes(_), Scope::RestrictedSelector(_)) | (Scope::RestrictedSelector(_), Scope::Hashes(_)) => false,` with module-docstring at lines 18-23 explaining the deferred-to-future-ratification rationale

The typed error returned is ChainNotNarrowing { step_index } — same as a genuinely-widening step. Audit consumers (or future debug tooling) get no signal that the failure is 'cross-arm-deferred' vs 'widening-real'

Per RATIFIED-S&C §R1 Path (a) only: cross-arm comparability is structurally a Path-(b) concern (the Hashes-arm IS effectively an opaque-selector if treated as comparable to a RestrictedSelector). Treating cross-arm as 'always non-narrowing' is the safe v1-beta choice — but the typed-reject conflates two semantic failures
findings.disposition: BELONGS-NAMED-NOW (V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE-DEFERRED.md row + future ChainValidationError::CrossArmNotComparable variant in v1-Composing)
